changed_line_after: shell += 'hepta_codec=$(CLASSPATH=' + shlex.quote(SCREEN_JAR) + ' app_process /system/bin org.trillionnium.hepta.screen.ScreenshotCodec ' + ' '.join(quoted) + ') || { hepta_codec_exit_code=$?; printf \'%s\' "$hepta_codec"; printf \'\\n{"schema":"hepta.codec-failure-observation.v1","codec_exit_code":%s,"codec_stdout_representation":"posix_shell_command_substitution_value","java_stdout_exact":false,"stderr_has_appended_diagnostic_record":true}\\n\' "$hepta_codec_exit_code" >&2; exit 72; }; '
observations: Only the existing codec command-substitution failure tail changes; guards, argv, token, image budgets, success envelope and EXIT cleanup trap are byte-identical.

The first failure-handler assignment captures the failed assignment's shell exit status before any printf. The quoted printf %s emits the shell variable value without adding an LF or re-evaluating its metacharacters.

The added stderr record is explicitly schema-tagged and reports codec exit status plus java_stdout_exact=false and the command-substitution representation. It is appended after a leading newline; existing stderr bytes are only a prefix of the resulting stream.

The failure block still requests exit 72. The untouched EXIT trap retains its existing ability to return 69 if PNG cleanup fails; this review does not assert unconditional 72 under every I/O or cleanup failure.

POSIX command substitution already removes trailing linefeeds and cannot establish byte-identical Java stdout; this is correctly disclosed. NUL handling, Android shell, SELinux, live codec behavior and transport limits were not exercised here.
No existing guard or budget constant changes. The extra failure output still has to fit the existing actual transport/output limits; no live retention or diagnostic-cause guarantee is made.
Changing production source bytes requires separately reviewed seal/combination/runtime/Root admission. This package is not a production rollout or a case qualification.
